lis.profile: Lis — a cool, deadpan, ironic street narrator of an adult comedy show about used-car flippers. Low calm voice, dry humor, confident.
lis.notes: Part 20 of a comedy mini-series about Tolyan building his own car dealership: the rival Zhora sets a trap — a too-cheap Camry sold by his nephew Vadik. Brisk, ironic narration with comic timing. Last line: a confident, warm advertising pitch for the bot «Перехват».

tolyan.profile: Tolyan — a cocky Russian used-car flipper (perekup) in his 30s, street swagger, deep raspy voice, show-off, calls everyone «брат». Adult street comedy.
tolyan.notes: No swearing. Line 1: suspicious, amused. Line 2: dry joke. Line 3: calm, firm, smug. Line 4: cheerful, mocking. Line 5: short, confident.

leha.profile: Lyokha — the most serious car dealer in Moscow: bald, tattooed, leather jacket, drives a Rolls-Royce. Low, heavy, calm, unhurried voice; speaks in short confident sentences like a mentor; dry humor.
leha.notes: No swearing. One line on a video call: calm, decisive, mentor-like warning.

vadik.profile: Vadik — Zhora's young nephew in his early 20s, a clumsy wannabe car hustler in a red cap; fast, pushy, nervous, bad liar. Adult street comedy.
vadik.notes: No swearing. Line 1: pushy, rushing the buyer. Line 2: caught off guard, awkward lie. Line 3: panicking, shouting into the phone.

rimma.profile: Rimma Zakharovna — a strict, businesslike Russian woman in her 50s who owns a former gas station lot; cool, precise, a little ironic, always calls Tolyan by his full name «Анатолий».
rimma.notes: One line: dry, strict, a deadline.
